verdict.rationale: Milvus's own reference docs say it supports four multi-tenancy strategies that trade off scalability, data isolation and flexibility, so tenant isolation is a first-party capability. RBAC scoped at the collection, database and instance levels backs up the isolation boundaries. However, the evidence does not name the strategies (partitions, per-tenant collections or databases), does not show they are cheap at scale, and states no tenant-count or resource limits. Missing for 10: explicit naming of the partition, collection and database strategies; documented per-strategy tenant limits; evidence of cost-efficiency at high tenant counts; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can isolate many tenants cheaply using namespaces, partitions, or per-tenant collections with documented limits

citations.quote: Milvus supports four multi-tenancy strategies, each offering a different trade-off between scalability, data isolation, and flexibility.
With RBAC, you can finely control the operations users can perform at the collection, database, and instance levels, enhancing data security.
